proof: Issuance serializes decisions with an exclusive ledger lock and refuses a second decision while an active one exists for the same exact seven-field binding, so two concurrent decisions with distinct verdict IDs and distinct nonces still admit exactly one durable verdict regardless of whether they agree.

A decision leaves the active set only through explicit revocation or its own expiry, so an exact replacement is admitted in those two cases and refused otherwise; an unreadable expiry is treated as active so the guard fails closed.
Consumption derives a deterministic idempotency key for the same logical transition retry while rejecting a distinct attempt as replay.

Missing or invalid policy, caller-controlled policy substitution, unauthorized role, fleet actor identity, missing MFA, rejected decision, revoked verdict, expiry, staleness, signature tamper, binding mismatch, unsafe path, and ledger symlink all fail closed.
Deleting mutable loop_ids or non_goals cannot remove the canonical protected-closeout audit.

Canonical JSON signing binds catalog digest, task ID, closeout manifest SHA, target environment, frontend deployment SHA, backend deployment SHA, decision, issuer, key ID, nonce, issuance time, and expiry.
Task state records the consumed ledger record ID, verdict digest, and idempotency key; the closeout guard compares all three with the authoritative consumption record.
A new ProductCloseoutVerdictService instance reloads the external fsynced JSONL ledger and preserves issued, revoked, nonce, and consumed state across process restart.
The same terminal operation can retry after restart using its deterministic idempotency key, and a consumed verdict remains auditable after issuance TTL at the recorded consumption time.
An authorized Human/Ops actor can revoke an unconsumed verdict; a consumed verdict cannot be revoked or reused.
A later exact valid verdict can supersede an expired or revoked task reference without weakening validation of the replacement.

environment_boundary.proof: The repository contains no live key, policy, ledger, credential, or verdict; absent protected external configuration fails closed.

mfa.proof: The BFF and governance layers require the authenticated MFA value to be exactly true before issuance or revocation.

no_live_capital.proof: The implementation controls task closeout only and grants no broker, allocation, deployment, runtime-control, or capital mutation authority.

rbac.proof: Only configured Human/Ops roles can issue or revoke, known fleet identities are denied independently of claimed role, and the BFF requires an explicit trusted human principal classification instead of inferring one: a session whose classification claim is missing, blank, unknown, or self-conflicting is refused even when it carries an admin role and verified MFA.

tenant_isolation.proof: The closeout verdict is a global program-control record rather than tenant data; tenant isolation is outside this task's data boundary.

two_person_approval.proof: Owner Claude and reviewer Codex2 are distinct and match both the assignment-revision-1 catalog and the canonical ai-status.json assignment. Owner evidence does not count as the formal reviewer verdict; the guard requires an approved Codex2 record before done.

acceptance.statement: Only an authenticated authorized Human or Ops actor can issue the final verdict.
The verdict binds the exact program catalog, task, closeout manifest, target, frontend, and backend identities.
Review-approved and done transitions fail closed for missing, rejected, revoked, replayed, stale, expired, tampered, unconsumed, or mismatched verdicts.
Fleet workers and candidate-controlled files or task metadata cannot self-sign or bypass protected authority.
Tamper, replay, wrong-role, wrong-task, wrong-SHA, expiry, revocation, concurrent-decision, direct-state-edit, and alternate-transition negatives pass.
